style_prompt: Bright indie folk-pop duet with acoustic guitar, brushed drums, light hand percussion, warm bass, close harmonies, and a natural live-room feel. The song should feel sunny, conversational, and commercially safe, with a memorable refrain and no named recording artists.
lyrics:
Verse 1
You sent a postcard from the coast
Salt on the ink, a faded note
I read it twice beneath the fan
Like summer waiting in my hands

Chorus
Meet me where the daylight bends
Where the road runs out and the blue begins
We can start with a simple line
Your hand in mine, your hand in mine

Verse 2
I kept the ticket from the train
A paper moon, a window frame
You laughed and said the world was wide
I said I only need this ride

Chorus
Meet me where the daylight bends
Where the road runs out and the blue begins
We can start with a simple line
Your hand in mine, your hand in mine

Bridge
No rush to name what we become
Just two voices chasing sun

Final Chorus
Meet me where the daylight bends
Where the road runs out and the blue begins
We can start with a simple line
Your hand in mine, your hand in mine
